title: 792. Valid Tic-Tac-Toe State

examples.explanation: The first mark must be X, so a lone O is impossible.
Four X against one O violates strict alternation.
Five X and four O with no line is a complete draw.

hints: Count the marks first: O can never outnumber X, and X can lead by at most one because X moves first.
Scan the eight possible lines for an X win and an O win; both winning together is always illegal.
An X win needs exactly one extra X, while an O win needs equal counts, since the winner made the final move. Adaptation: empty is '-'.
